dish: Whole wood-fired crispy snapper for build-your-own tacos
w: Mexican seafood house tucked into Thalia Hall from the Obelix / Taqueria Chingón team — whole fish from a wood-burning oven with tortillas and salsas.

dish: Chef Thai Dang's caramelized-pork and whole-fish Vietnamese plates
w: Chef Thai Dang's 'unapologetically authentic' Vietnamese dining room in Pilsen — a James Beard-semifinalist kitchen and neighbourhood mainstay.

dish: Pan dulce — conchas, empanadas, Día de Reyes rosca
w: Pilsen's beloved ~50-year-old panadería — trays of conchas, cookies and fruit empanadas; its Three Kings roscas made the Sun-Times in 2026.

dish: Chicken thighs in mole negro; chorizo-and-chihuahua breakfast sandwich at brunch
w: Latina-owned open-kitchen Mexican spot — seasonal mole and chile-laced beef soup, spice-adjustable margaritas, a strong Sunday brunch.

address: W Taylor St, Little Italy, Chicago
dish: Square Italian bakery-style pizza (since 1909)
w: Fourth-generation Taylor Street institution that grew from a 1909 bakery — still turning out thick, square bakery-style slices and hearty Italian-American plates.

dish: Rotating seasonal French bistro classics on Little Italy's best patio
w: French bistro hidden off the Taylor Street bustle — a locals' and critics' favourite with the neighbourhood's best patio and a deep wine list.

dish: Lamb barbacoa and duck-and-pork chorizo tacos
w: Evanston's taco-and-margarita stalwart — a dozen tacos, three to an order, with family-style beans and rice.

dish: Ropa vieja empanadas; sweet-potato and yucca-chimichurri tacos
w: Small carry-out that grew out of the Evanston farmers' market — Latin American burritos, gorditas and empanadas with smart vegetarian fillings.

address: 4248 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60653
dish: The 'sauced six' wings (mango habanero, sweet red chili, spiced bourbon) with gold corn muffin
w: Chef Kristen Harper's Creole-leaning Bronzeville soul-food counter — some of Chicago's best wings and fried chicken; Keith Lee's only 10/10 on his 2023 Chicago tour.

address: S Cottage Grove Ave at E 44th St, Bronzeville, Chicago, IL 60653
dish: Chili-oil crispy brussels sprouts with a wine list of women, minority and Black winemakers
w: Black-owned wine bar-restaurant from the Silver Room's owner — art-hung room, DJs and live music, a list that champions minority-owned producers.

dish: Specialty burgers, shakes and pastries from the Medici bakery
w: The 'Med' — UChicago's hangout since 1963, booths carved with students' poetry and political rants; a breakfast-to-late menu.

dish: Handmade broth-filled dumplings — lamb & dill, lobster & pork, crab roe; steamed, boiled or fried
w: Chinatown's dumpling specialist, risen from a Richland Center basement stand — ~40 fillings in three cooking styles, more varieties than anywhere in Chicago.

dish: Handmade xiao long bao (pork, crab or chicken), folded in the front window
w: Chinatown's soup-dumpling specialist — xiaolongbao made fresh daily in full view of the dining room.

address: 5200 S Archer Ave, Unit 8, Chicago, IL 60632
dish: Mexico City-style tlacoyos on house masa (cochinita pibil, squash blossom)
w: Family-run Archer Heights counter where scratch masa is the star — tlacoyos, picaditas, sopes and giant quesadillas (Infatuation 9.4).

dish: Al pastor sliced to order from the trompo; 'El Toro' (pastor + chorizo + pineapple + habanero)
w: Little Village taqueria that grew from Adan Lucido's home pop-up — al pastor carved to order off the spit with pineapple and salsa.

dish: Rib tips ('meat candy'), brisket, oxtail gumbo, sweet-potato cornbread
w: Beverly's Texas-style smokehouse — on the New York Times' 2025 list of the 50 best US restaurants and Jean Banchet Best Counter Service 2026.

dish: Strawberry-basil key lime pie; quiches and chicken pot pie
w: James Beard-finalist baker Maya-Camille Broussard's social-mission pie shop in a former dentist's office on 87th Street.

dish: House beers and wood-fired pizza on the rooftop beer garden
w: Beverly's brewpub — a South Side destination for its beer, wood-fired pizza and 1,900 sq ft rooftop beer garden (new owners since May 2024).

dish: Steak dinners and a big Southern brunch
w: Roseland steakhouse since 1969, Black-owned since 2018 — reopened in 2022 after the 2020 fire and looting.

dish: Experimental house beers with Taco Sublime's fried-cheese tacos and smashburgers
w: McKinley Park warehouse taproom from the Maria's/Kimski family — wraparound bar, brewhouse views, arcade, karaoke and comedy nights.

dish: Durango-style charred burritos and gorditas; horchata in a giant mug
w: Tiny McKinley Park family kitchen for Durango street food — svelte griddle-charred burritos and stuffed gorditas.
